rationale: The paused TimeoutNow lead was narrowed by source reading into a sharper hypothesis on the same code path: when a leadership transfer is interrupted (the starting leader loses leadership while the transfer is draining replication to the target), the transfer goroutine's drain loop can be left blocked sending to the followerReplication's triggerDeferErrorCh once that replicator has exited, and because the outer transfer goroutine waits on doneCh before its deferred setLeadershipTransferInProgress(false) runs, the in-progress flag would stay set. getLeadershipTransferInProgress gates every client entry point of a leader (Apply, config changes, restore, GetConfiguration), and setLeadershipTransferInProgress(false) appears only in that deferred call, so a stuck flag would leave a re-elected node permanently rejecting client writes. A first local probe (native feedback, not retained evidence) did not exercise the mechanism at all because the target was up to date, so the transfer completed before any interruption; a corrected local probe added a real replication backlog and partitioned the leader, which did run the drain loop and made the transfer time out, yet the flag cleared in all ten trials. This submission registers that hypothesis as an active child question with its discriminator and submits the corrected probe for retained execution, so the claim is either carried by a receipt or honestly refuted.

investigations.question: If a leadership transfer is interrupted while its drain loop still has replication work, can the transfer goroutine be stranded on the followerReplication triggerDeferErrorCh send so that the deferred setLeadershipTransferInProgress(false) never runs, leaving a node that later becomes leader permanently rejecting client operations with ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress?
investigations.hypothesis: The drain loop sends a deferError on repl.triggerDeferErrorCh outside any arm on the transfer's stop channel, and the only reader of that channel is the peer's replication goroutine, which exits when the leader steps down (runLeader's defer closes its stopCh) or when the peer is removed. If the leader loses leadership between the goroutine's wake-up and that send, the send has no reader and blocks forever; the outer transfer goroutine then blocks on doneCh before its deferred setLeadershipTransferInProgress(false), so the flag stays set for the lifetime of the Raft instance, including after a later election of that instance.
investigations.discriminator: Run a real three-voter cluster, isolate the transfer target, commit a backlog that the target never receives, start a transfer to that target, then cut the starting leader off so it steps down while the transfer is draining. Predict: the transfer future resolves with an error, the drained goroutine is left in the triggerDeferErrorCh send, getLeadershipTransferInProgress stays true, and after the old leader is made leader again through a normal transfer its Apply and GetConfiguration return ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress. A control trial without the interruption must show the flag cleared and client calls unaffected; if every interrupted trial clears the flag with no stranded goroutine, the hypothesis is defeated for this trigger.

scope.description: Twelve trials (ten interrupted, two control) over real three-voter clusters with the in-memory transport: in the interrupted trials the transfer target is isolated, a backlog is committed that the target never receives, a leadership transfer to that target is started, and the starting leader is then isolated so it steps down while the transfer still has replication work; the partition is healed, the rest of the cluster elects, and the interrupted node is made leader again through a normal transfer so its client entry points can be exercised.
assumptions: In-memory transport with the captured in-memory timeouts (50ms heartbeat/election/lease), so the interruption and step-down happen within milliseconds; this is the same facility the target's own tests use.

LeadershipTransferToServer is the documented client contract for starting a transfer; isolating the leader is a permitted environment event, and the target's step-down follows from its own lease check.
In the control trials the same transfer runs with no interruption and no backlog, so a trial-level difference is attributable to the interruption rather than to the transfer itself.
The observed flag and state are read through the same in-package accessors the target's own tests use; the client-visible endpoints are Apply and GetConfiguration.
excluded: No on-disk log store, no network transport and no multi-process execution: the mechanism under test is the transfer goroutine's interaction with leadership loss, not storage or sockets.
No attempt is made to widen the race window artificially, for example by pausing goroutines or by modifying production code.

parameters.timing: target isolated, backlog committed, transfer started, leader isolated after 30ms, 300ms settle, heal, then wait up to 3s for another leader and up to 2s for the re-election
parameters.recorded: trial, mode, leader and target IDs, last index of each at transfer time, transfer future error, transfer_in_progress_after, new leader found, re-elected, Apply error, GetConfiguration error, stranded transfer stack frames

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds a real three-voter cluster through MakeCluster with an in-memory transport and the captured in-memory timeouts, takes the elected leader and a follower target, isolates the target with the cluster Partition helper, and commits a 200-command backlog through the leader's normal Apply path so the leader's log is ahead of the target and replication to it cannot succeed. It records both last indexes, starts a transfer to the target with LeadershipTransferToServer, waits 30ms so the drain loop is running, then isolates the starting leader so that it loses quorum contact and steps down while the transfer still has work. After 300ms it heals the partitions, waits for a leader among the remaining nodes, reads the transfer flag through the in-package accessor, samples goroutine stacks for a goroutine left in the leadership transfer path, and finally makes the interrupted node leader again with a normal transfer from the current leader and calls Apply and GetConfiguration on it, recording the exact errors. Control trials run the transfer without any partition or backlog. Only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected and no production file is modified.
